flawed_step: lines 0061-0063 ("In either case, S ... crucially no neighbor in W_m (since S ⊇ R_{m-1} ...)")
reasoning_summary: L0002-0004 (strategy: proof by contradiction using expansion) — no mathematical claim, acceptable framing. L0005-0006 (base case k=2 statement: an edge between W1 and W2 exists) — correct statement to prove. L0007 (assume for contradiction no W1-W2 edge) — valid contradiction hypothesis. L0008-0011 (pick S ⊆ W1 with |S| = n/2, justified by "|W1| > n/2 when α > 0") — conclusion is fine but the stated justification is wrong: α > 0 makes (1-α)n smaller, not larger; what is needed is α ≤ 1/2, which does follow from the hypothesis since |N(S)| ≤ n forces n/2 + αn ≤ n (and at α = 1/2 one only gets |W1| ≥ n/2, still enough); minor justification slip, not fatal. L0011-0013 (no edges W1-W2 ⇒ N(S) ∩ W2 = ∅ ⇒ N(S) ⊆ V\W2, and |V\W2| ≤ αn) — correct, uses S ⊆ W1 and |W2| ≥ (1-α)n. L0014-0018 (|N(S)| ≤ αn contradicts |N(S)| ≥ n/2 + αn) — correct; base case established. L0019-0021 (setup for k ≥ 3, assume no valid path exists) — valid contradiction hypothesis. L0022-0024 (layered digraph; base case gives at least one edge between consecutive layers) — true but vacuous here: the existence of a single W_i-W_{i+1} edge is never used in the rest of the argument, so labelling this an "inductive step" is misleading though harmless. L0025-0037 (BFS definition R_1 := W_1, R_i := N(R_{i-1}) ∩ W_i as the layered-reachable sets) — well-defined and matches the intended semantics. L0038-0040 (no path ⇒ R_k = ∅; let m be minimal with R_m = ∅, so 2 ≤ m ≤ k) — correct: any v ∈ R_k can be back-traced to a full path, and R_1 = W_1 ≠ ∅ (W_1 nonempty since (1-α)n > 0). L0041-0047 (R_1,...,R_{m-1} nonempty; every v ∈ R_{m-1} has no neighbor in W_m) — correct, immediate from R_m = N(R_{m-1}) ∩ W_m = ∅. L0048-0053 (case |R_{m-1}| ≥ n/2: take S ⊆ R_{m-1} with |S| = n/2) — valid; here N(S) ⊆ N(R_{m-1}) really is disjoint from W_m. L0054-0060 (case |R_{m-1}| < n/2: pad R_{m-1} with arbitrary vertices of W_{m-1} to get R_{m-1} ⊆ S ⊆ W_{m-1}, |S| = n/2; "no vertex in S lies in W_m (indeed S ⊆ W_{m-1})") — the padding is possible (|W_{m-1}| ≥ n/2), but the parenthetical is a further error: the W_i are not assumed disjoint, so S ⊆ W_{m-1} does not imply S ∩ W_m = ∅ (and set membership was never what the argument needed anyway). L0061-0063 (FIRST FATAL STEP: "In either case ... S has no neighbor in W_m, since S ⊇ R_{m-1} and R_{m-1} has no edges to W_m") — non sequitur: enlarging a set enlarges its neighborhood, so N(S) ⊇ N(R_{m-1}) gives no upper bound; in the padded case the vertices of S \ R_{m-1} are arbitrary members of W_{m-1} that are simply unreachable from W_1, and nothing forbids them from having many neighbors in W_m (indeed under the true hypotheses they must). The whole case |R_{m-1}| < n/2 is therefore unsupported. L0064-0067 (N(S) ⊆ V\W_m hence |N(S)| ≤ αn) — arithmetic is right but inherits the unjustified premise in case 2. L0068-0071 (contradiction with |N(S)| ≥ n/2 + αn) — valid only in case 1. L0072-0076 (conclude a path exists) — unsound, since the contradiction was never derived when |R_{m-1}| < n/2. Note the statement itself is true — the standard fix is to prove |R_i| ≥ n/2 for all i by induction (if |R_{i-1}| ≥ n/2, take S ⊆ R_{i-1} of size n/2, then |R_i| ≥ |N(S) ∩ W_i| ≥ (n/2 + αn) - αn = n/2), which is exactly the gap this proof papers over by padding S with unreachable vertices.
